main_body: Tall brick townhouse: slate mansard roof with a dormer and chimney, an orange cornice, three brick storeys with framed windows and a balcony, and a green door at ground level
top_band: Slate roof band, blue-grey, rows ~10-42: a flat roof top with a dark rim (rows 10-24), a lighter slate lip (rows 22-26), then shingled slope with a dormer (rows 26-42). The orange cornice sits at rows 42-46.
evidence: Reading down the middle column, the slate roof is a clearly drawn sloped surface (about 16 rows of shingles plus the flat roof top above). Below it the orange cornice at rows 42-46 acts as the front-edge line and a dark shadow row sits under it. The brick front face then runs about 96 rows. Windows have stone frames with inset dark glass, and the balcony projects with a dark underside. This reads like the reference houses, whose roofs are visible slopes above vertical walls, so it is a 3/4 building rather than a flat elevation.

style.evidence: Brick has about 5 tones with per-brick highlights and mortar variation. The slate has several tones with shingle rows, and the stone window frames and trims are shaded. Outlines lean dark blue or brown next to their material and are not pure black. The glowing windows and the balcony railing add a lot of colour per tile. No large flat fills. It is comparable to the Beodeul house references in density.
